questions.question: Which law of economics state "Bad money drives out good money"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gresham's Law**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gresham's Law:** 

 
 
• Named after** Sir Thomas Gresham**, a financial adviser to **Queen Elizabeth I, Gresham's Law** is an economic principle that states: "when two types of commodity money of equal face value but different intrinsic values are in circulation, the commodity with the lesser intrinsic value will remain in circulation, while the commodity of greater intrinsic value will be hoarded and disappear from circulation." 
 
• Essentially, this means "bad money drives out good money".
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ohm's Law: **

 
 
• This is a fundamental concept in physics and electrical engineering.
 
• Formulated by German physicist George Simon Ohm, this law states that the current passing through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points, provided the temperature remains constant.
 
• The law is usually expressed as I=V/R, where I is current, V is voltage, and R is resistance.
 
 
 
• **Gauss's Law: **
 
 
• Named after the German mathematician and physicist Carl Friedrich Gauss, Gauss's Law is a law in electrostatics that states that the total flux of the electric field E over a closed surface is equal to 1/ε times the charge enclosed by the surface.
 
• It is one of Maxwell's four equations, which form the basis of classical electrodynamics.
 
 
 
• **Baxter's Law:**
 
 
• Baxter's Law is not a widely recognized or accepted principle in any major field of study.
 
• There are references to "Baxter's Law" in popular culture and literature, but these should not be confused with the formally recognized laws in fields like physics or economics.
 
• Depending on the context, it may have different implications, but it's not an established law in disciplines such as economics or physics.

questions.question: When did Mahatma Gandhi founded the All India Harijan Sevak Sangh?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1932**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Mahatma Gandhi founded the All India Harijan Sevak Sangh on 30th September 1932.
 
• The organization was established to work for upliftment and welfare of the socially and economically downtrodden section of the society, particularly the Dalit community, who were then referred to as Harijans, meaning "children of God".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi, also known as **Mahatma Gandhi, was born on October 2, 1869, in Porbandar, Gujarat, India**.
 
• During his time in **South Africa**, from **1893 to 1914**, he developed his political views, ethics, and political leadership skills.
 
• He introduced the term** "Satyagraha" (devotion to truth),** which signified nonviolent resistance as a means of protest.
 
• Upon returning to **India in 1915,** he joined the Indian National Congress, beginning his active involvement in India's fight for independence.
 
• He led numerous campaigns against the **British rule, including the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1920, the Salt March in 1930, and the Quit India Movement in 1942.**
 
• Gandhi adopted a simple lifestyle, which included wearing traditional Indian clothing, eating a vegetarian diet, and practicing daily meditation.
 
• He strongly advocated for unity between **Hindus and Muslims, which was a major issue in Indian politics at the time.**
 
• Gandhi was a major advocate for **untouchables (Dalits), whom he called Harijans or "children of god".**
 
• He worked to end social discrimination against them and campaigned for their civil rights.
 
• He was key in helping India achieve independence from British rule.
 
• India was officially declared independent at midnight on **August 15, 1947**.
 
• Unfortunately, Mahatma Gandhi was assassinated in **New Delhi **on **January 30, 1948, by Nathuram Godse, a radical Hindu nationalist.**
 
• **Gandhi's philosophy of nonviolent resistance inspired future human rights movements around the world, earning him the title "Mahatma", which means "great soul".**

questions.question: The feature of Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution is borrowed from the ________ Constitution
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Irish**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Irish Constitution:**
 
• It served as the model for the **Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution.**
 
• These principles are guidelines for the Indian government in terms of the socio-economic policies that it should adopt, and though not **justiciable, (i.e., enforceable by courts), **they are considered fundamental in the governance of the country.
 
• **Ireland's constitution, Bunreacht na hÉireann, enacted in 1937**, also contains Directive Principles of Social Policy, designed to guide legal decision-making and the legislative process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **French Constitution:**
 
• India borrowed the ideals of **Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity from the French Constitution.**
 
• These principles now form part of the Preamble to the Indian Constitution.
 
• **Canadian Constitution:**
 
• The provisions related to a federation with a strong central government, the division of powers between the central and state governments, and the advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court were borrowed from the Canadian constitution.
 
• **British Constitution: **
 
• From the British Constitution, India derived numerous key administrative details, including the rule of law, the parliamentary system of **governance, the law-making procedures, single citizenship, and the establishment of the office of the Comptroller and Auditor General.**

questions.question: Lok Sabha has a fixed term of ______ years and can be dissolved by the President at any time.

• The term of a member of parliament of Lok Sabha (dissolved) is five years from the date appointed for its first meeting.
 
• During a state of emergency, the term however can be extended by the Parliament of India by law for a period not exceeding one year at a time.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The 1st Lok Sabha was constituted on 17 April 1952 and had 489 constituencies, thereby the first set of elected members of parliament of Lok Sabha in India.
 
• The maximum permitted strength of members of parliament in the Lok Sabha is 550.
 
• The first instance of a member of parliament equivalent in India dates back to 9 December 1946, the day the Constituent Assembly of India was formed with the purpose of drafting a constitution for India.

questions.question: _____ is the heaviest naturally occuring element of Periodic Table with an atomic weight of 238.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Uranium__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Uranium

 
 
• It is a silvery-white metallic chemical element in the periodic table, with atomic number 92.
 
• It is assigned the chemical symbol U. A uranium atom has 92 protons and 92 electrons, of which 6 are valence electrons.
 
• Uranium has the highest atomic weight (19 kg m) of all naturally occurring elements.
 
• The heaviest element discovered is Ununoctium or Organesson with atomic number 118 but it is man-made.
 
• The heaviest naturally occurring element is Uranium with atomic number 92 and atomic weight 238 gm.
 
• The repulsive force of 118's positively charged protons put enormous pressure on the nucleus, and it lasted for a little under a millisecond before splitting itself into lighter nuclei.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

** Helium**

 
• Helium is a chemical element with the symbol** He** and atomic number **2.** It is a **colorless, odorless, tasteless, non-toxic, inert, monatomic gas** that heads the noble gas group in the periodic table. Its boiling and melting points are the lowest among the elements and it exists only as a gas except in extreme conditions.
 
• Helium was discovered in the solar spectrum by **Pierre Janssen** during the solar eclipse of **1868** and was named after the Greek word** "Helios"**, which means **Sun.**

** Xenon**

 
• Xenon is a chemical element with the symbol** Xe** and atomic number **54.** It is a **colorless, heavy, odorless **noble gas found in the Earth's atmosphere in trace amounts. The element is generally used in light-emitting devices called xenon flash lamps and as a general anesthetic.

** Mercury**

 
• Mercury is a chemical element with the symbol **Hg **and atomic number **80.** It is commonly known as **quicksilver** and was formerly named** hydrargyrum**. Mercury is the only metallic element that is liquid at standard conditions for temperature and pressure.

questions.question: Which famous Indian Kathak dancer received the Padma Vibhushan, India's second highest civilian award, in 1986?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Birju Maharaj.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pandit Birju Maharaj **was an Indian dancer, composer, singer, and exponent of the Lucknow "Kalka-Bindadin" Gharana of Kathak dance in India.
 
• He was a descendant of the Maharaj family of Kathak dancers, which includes his two uncles, Shambhu Maharaj and Lachhu Maharaj, and his father and guru, Acchan Maharaj.
 
• He was born on 4 February 1938 in Handia and died on 17 January 2022 in Delhi.
 
• He was awarded Padma Vibhushan and Filmfare Award for Best Choreography and more.
 
• Kathak is one of the eight major forms of Indian classical dance. It is the classical dance form of Uttar Pradesh. The origin of Kathak is traditionally attributed to the traveling bards of ancient northern India known as Kathakars or storytellers.
 
• He received the ‘**Padma Vibhushan**’ in 1986.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Mallika Sarabhai**

__
 
• She is an Indian classical dancer, choreographer, actress, writer, and social activist known for her promotion of the arts as a vehicle for social change.
 
• Mallika is an accomplished Kuchipudi and Bharatanatyam dancer and performer who has specialized in using the arts for social change and transformation.
 
• She started to learn dancing when she was young and started her film career in the parallel cinema when she was 15.
 
• Mallika played the role of Draupadi in Peter Brook's play The Mahabharata.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Padma Awards**

 
 
• Padma Awards one of the highest civilian Awards in the country are conferred in three categories, namely, Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan and Padma Shri.
 
• The Awards are given in various disciplines/ fields of activities,
 
 
• Art, social work, public affairs, science and engineering, trade and industry, medicine, literature and education, sports, civil service, etc.
 
 
 
• Padma Vibhushan is awarded for exceptional and distinguished service.
 
• Padma Bhushan for distinguished service of a high order.
 
• Padma Shri for distinguished service in any field.
 
• The awards are announced on the occasion of Republic Day every year. 
 
• These awards are conferred by the **President of India.**

questions.question: The Blackbuck National Park is located in _______
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Gujarat__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Blackbuck National Park is located in Gujarat.
 
• The sanctuary was established in July 1976, as an initial protected area of about 18 sq km.
 
• In 1980, another 16 sq km were added to increase the total area to 34 sq km.
 
• The park is surrounded Gulf of Khambhat on the south and by wastelands and agriculture fields on the other sides.
 
• It was the grassland of the Maharaja of the princely state of Bhavnagar.
 
• The National park has been classified as a 4B Gujarat-Rajwada biotic province of a semi-arid bio-geographical zone.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The top 5 National Parks of Gujarat for Wildlife Sanctuaries are:

 
 
• Gir National Park.
 
• Marine National Park.
 
• Jambughoda Wildlife Sanctuary.
 
• Barda Wildlife Sanctuary.
 
• Purna Wildlife Sanctuary.
